o: Compare the sum of digits at even indices with the sum at odd indices. '1234' gives 1+3=4 vs 2+4=6 → false; '24123' gives 6 vs 6 → true. With length ≤ 100 a single pass with two accumulators is everything the constraints demand.
k: One pass with two accumulators (even-index sum, odd-index sum) solves it directly.
Parity of the index, not parity of the digit, decides the bucket.

a.n: Approach 1: Single Pass with Two Accumulators
a.i: Iterate once, adding each digit to the even or odd sum based on index parity, then compare.
s: For each index i, add digit to even if i is even else odd.
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the digits.

a.i: Equivalently, the string is balanced when the alternating signed digit sum is zero, expressible as a one-line slice sum or a reduce with sign (+1, −1 alternating).
s: Compute sum of digits at even indices minus sum at odd indices.
Return whether the difference is zero.
a.t: O(n) — still a single pass (the Python slice version makes two).
a.sp: O(n) for the Python slices; O(1) for the C++/Java signed-sum variants.

w: Trivial warm-up; the only traps are confusing digit parity with index parity and off-by-one at the start. Follow-up: minimum insertions/deletions to balance the string, or balance over base-b digits.
